cade.reason: The libfix clipped from `cavalcade` -- `autocade`, `aquacade`, `motorcade`. The dictionary's free `cade` (a juniper, or a hand-reared lamb) is a homograph none of them is built on.

carpous.reason: Greek -karpos (fruit), only ever a final element -- `pseudocarpous`, `monocarpous`, `syncarpous`.

chromy.reason: Greek -chromia, only ever a final element -- `photochromy`, `polychromy`, `heliochromy`.

cide.reason: Latin -cida/-cidium (killing), only ever a final element -- `autocide`, `suicide`, `pesticide`.

crat.reason: Greek -krates (ruler), only ever a final element -- `monocrat`, `technocrat`, `bureaucrat`.

duce.reason: Latin ducere (to lead), only ever a final element -- `subduce`, `traduce`, `abduce`.

genically.reason: The bound -genic plus -ally. `telegenically` is `telegenic` + -ally, and no part of it is a word on its own.

genies.reason: Plural of the bound -geny, not of `genie`. `monogenies` is a theory of single origin; the lamp-dweller is a homograph and the worst base this table could hand a player.

genous.reason: Greek -genes (produced by), only ever a final element -- `monogenous`, `endogenous`, `indigenous`.

geny.reason: Greek -geneia (origin), only ever a final element -- `monogeny`, `ontogeny`, `phylogeny`.

gol.reason: The tail of `hypergol` (a self-igniting propellant), from Greek ergon. Not a word.

graphy.reason: Greek -graphia (writing), only ever a final element -- `macrography`, `photography`, `biography`. Heads 197 dictionary entries and is a word in none of them.

istic.reason: The -istic adjective ending, which the dictionary lists as an entry. `ultraistic` is `ultraist` + -ic; 364 words end this way and none is built on a word called `istic`.

lect.reason: Latin legere (to read/gather), only ever a final element -- `prelect`, `dialect`, `intellect`.

lector.reason: Agent noun on the bound -lect. `prelector` is one who prelects, not one who `lectors`.

lith.reason: Greek lithos (stone), only ever a final element -- `neolith`, `monolith`, `batholith`, `otolith`. The single clearest case for this table: 27 dictionary entries end in it and none of them is built on a word called `lith`. (`lithic` is a different matter -- that one is a real adjective and folds normally.)

logy.reason: Greek -logia, only ever a final element -- `antilogy`, `biology`, `geology`. English does have a free `logy` (sluggish, from Dutch), but it is a homograph and not what any of the 414 words ending this way are built on.

merous.reason: Greek -meres (parted), only ever a final element -- `polymerous`, `pentamerous`, `dimerous`.

metrist.reason: Agent noun on the bound -metry -- `photometrist`, `optometrist`, `posologist`'s cousin. Never free.

mune.reason: Latin munire (to fortify), the tail of `premune`/`premunition`. Not a word.

nomen.reason: Latin nomen (name) as a final element -- `prenomen`, `cognomen`, `agnomen`.

ologist.reason: The -ologist agent ending, which the dictionary lists as an entry. 279 words end this way -- `misologist`, `biologist`, `geologist` -- and none is built on a word called `ologist`. `derivedBaseCandidates` already folds these to their -ology, which is the right base.

ology.reason: Greek -logia with its connecting vowel, only ever a final element -- `misology`, `biology`, `theology`. English does have a jocular free `ology` (`all the -ologies`), but it is a back-formation from the ending and not what any compound is built on.

onymous.reason: Greek -onymos (named), only ever a final element -- `polyonymous`, `anonymous`, `synonymous`.

parous.reason: Latin -parus (bearing), only ever a final element -- `nonparous`, `multiparous`, `oviparous`.

pathy.reason: Greek -patheia (feeling/suffering), only ever a final element -- `protopathy`, `sympathy`, `neuropathy`.

ped.reason: Latin pes/pedis (foot) as a final element -- `multiped`, `biped`, `quadruped`. The dictionary's free `ped` (a pannier; a clipping of pedestrian) is a homograph none of those is built on.

pede.reason: The -ped foot element with its Latin ending -- `multipede`, `centipede`, `millipede`.

phile.reason: Greek philos (loving), only ever a final element -- `neophile`, `bibliophile`, `audiophile`.

philia.reason: Greek -philia (affinity), only ever a final element -- `neophilia`, `haemophilia`.

phyte.reason: Greek phyton (plant), only ever a final element -- `autophyte`, `epiphyte`, `neophyte`.

phytic.reason: The bound -phyte plus -ic -- `autophytic`, `microphytic`, `neophytic`. A combining form that reaches six letters by taking a suffix of its own is still a combining form. (The unrelated `phytic acid` is a homograph.)

pode.reason: Greek pous/podos (foot), only ever a final element -- `monopode`, `antipode`, `arthropod`'s cousin.

pone.reason: Latin ponere (to place), only ever a final element -- `prepone`, `postpone`, `depone`. The dictionary's free `pone` (corn bread) is a homograph none of those is built on.

reges.reason: Latin plural of rex, carried into `interreges`. Not an English word in any use.

stich.reason: Greek stichos (a line of verse), only ever a final element -- `monostich`, `telestich`, `hemistich`.

stome.reason: Greek stoma (mouth), only ever a final element -- `monostome`, `cyclostome`.

therian.reason: Greek therion (beast), only ever a final element -- `prototherian`, `metatherian`, `eutherian`.

typy.reason: The -typy process ending -- `phototypy`, `linotypy`, `stereotypy`. The dictionary's free `typy` (of livestock, true to type) is a homograph none of those is built on.

zoarium.reason: Greek -zoarion (colony of zooids), only ever a final element -- `polyzoarium`.

zoic.reason: Greek -zoikos (of animals), only ever a final element -- `polyzoic`, `protozoic`, `Palaeozoic`.
